title: Package superseded status and the mock functions
description:
The [v0.4.5](https://github.com/r-lib/mockery/releases/tag/v0.4.5) release has marked the lifecycle for this package as superseded. In particular, the readme states

> This package is superseded and we no longer recommend that you use it for new tests. We instead recommend testthat::local_mocked_bindings().

How does this affect the `mock()` function and its associated `expect_` functions? I can't see any reason why the `mock` function would pose any issues going forwards, but there is no clear alternative to `mock` in other packages.

title: with_mock() is going away (2)
description: This is a second reminder that `with_mock()` is going away in the next release of testthat, which I'm aiming to release October 1. The API functions that made it work are being removed in R 4.5.0, so we'd suggest that you switch to `with_mocked_bindings()/local_mocked_bindings()` instead.

title: with_mock() is going away
description: This is a heads up to let you know that `with_mock()` is deprecated and will be made defunct soon. The API functions that made it work are being removed in R 4.5.0, so we'd suggest that you switch to `with_mocked_bindings()` instead.

title: Stubbing destroys package methods
Strange behaviour when stubbing R6 classes in global environment - stub affects non-stubbed functions
description:
``` r
library(R6)
library(mockery)
library(openxlsx)

# Define public function
some_function = function() {
 cat("something")
}

# Define class "some_class"
some_class = R6Class("some_class",
                     public = list(
                       some_method = function() {return(some_function())},
                       other_method = function() {return('method in class')}
                     )
)

# Check we can initialise class and call method
obj = some_class$new()
obj$some_method() #works
#> something

# Now we stub the method `some_method`, but with a function that we don't even
# call in the method - "hi"

# This works inside a local(), but not outside...
local({
  stub(obj$some_method, 'hi', function() NULL)
  wb <- createWorkbook()
  addWorksheet(wb, "sheet1")
  writeData(wb, sheet = "sheet1", x = mtcars)
  saveWorkbook(wb, "test.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE) ## works inside local
})

unlink("test.xlsx")

# Doesn't work outside of local({})
stub(obj$some_method, 'hi', function() NULL)
wb <- createWorkbook()
addWorksheet(wb, "sheet1")
writeData(wb, sheet = "sheet1", x = mtcars)
saveWorkbook(wb, "test.xlsx", overwrite = TRUE) ## works inside local
#> Error in write_worksheet_xml(prior = prior, post = post, sheet_data = ws$sheet_data, : Evaluation error: <text>:1:28: unexpected '<'
#> 1: new("Sheet_Data", .xData = <
#>                                ^.
```

title: stub effects outside intended context
description:
I'm not sure if this is one bug or several (or zero!), but these are three bits of behavior I wasn't expecting that all came up while debugging one issue in my own code, so here they are together.

1. Stubs with depth > 1 remain in effect outside the function that defined them:
	```
	h = function()1
	g = function()h()
	f = function()g()

	test_that("stubbing works in a non-nested function", {
		expect_equal(g(), 1)
		stub(g, "h", 2)
		expect_equal(g(), 2)
	})
	test_that("stubs do not carry over between test blocks", {
		expect_equal(g(), 1)
	})

	test_that("stubbing works inside a nested function", {
		expect_equal(f(), 1)
		stub(f, "h", 2, depth=2)
		expect_equal(f(), 2) 
	})
	test_that("nested stubs do not carry over between test blocks", {
		expect_equal(f(), 1) # FAILS: h is still stubbed
	})
	```

2. Stubs with depth > 1 can affect calls not in `what`:
	```
	g = function(y) y
	f = function(x) g(x) + 1
	r = function(x) g(x) + f(x)
	test_that('only calls from what are stubbed', {
		stub(r, 'g', 100, depth=2)
		expect_equal(r(1), 201)
		expect_equal(g(1), 1)
		expect_equal(f(1), 2) # FAILS: uses stubbed g
	})
	```

3. When stubs are called from within functions defined outside of the test, only the first-defined stub is used:
	```
	f = function(x) x + 10
	g = function(y) y + 20
	h = function(z) f(z) + g(z)
	u = function(zz)h(zz)
	test_that('multiple stubs defined in test work with functions defined outside test', {
		
		u_local = function(zz)h(zz)

		stub(h, 'f', 300)
		stub(h, 'g', 500)

		expect_equal(h(1), 800)
		expect_equal(u_local(1), 800)
		expect_equal(u(1), 800) # FAILS: uses unstubbed version of g
	})
	```
	An apparent workaround is to define the stubs outside of the test function:
	```
	f = function(x) x + 10
	g = function(y) y + 20
	h = function(z) f(z) + g(z)
	u = function(zz)h(zz)
	stub(h, 'f', 300)
	stub(h, 'g', 500)
	test_that('multiple stubs defined outside of test work with functions defined outside test', {

		u_local = function(zz)h(zz)

		expect_equal(h(1), 800)
		expect_equal(u_local(1), 800)
		expect_equal(u(1), 800)
	})
	```

* * *

title: Trouble stubbing 2nd-level function that uses double colon for third call
description:
Hi Folks. (Sorry if the title is confusing - I didn't know what exactly to put.) I'm new to R and to mockery. Thanks for your work. After a lot of experimentation I've discovered behavior that seems like a bug to me, but it's entirely possible I'm missing something basic. It revolves around mocking a second-level function that calls another package's function using the double colon syntax to specify the namespace. In this case I have failed to find a way to get `stub()` to work. By accident I found I *am* able to stub the called function if I remove the namespace reference.

The following results are when there is no local development server running at :8000. "fails" means the function is not successfully mocked: GET is called but the connection is refused. "works" means GET is mocked, but then stop_for_status gets the expected error (I'm returning a string, not a proper response object).

I hope this is enough to demonstrate the problem I'm having. Thank you.


```R
# file 1: connection.R

mockery_bug <- function() {
  mockery_bug2()
}

mockery_bug2 <- function() {
  # response <- httr::GET(url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/")  # namespace -> cannot get stub to work
  response <- GET(url = "http://127.0.0.1:8000/")  # no namespace -> am able to get stub to work
  httr::stop_for_status(response)
}
```


```R
# file 2: test_connection.R

test_that("mockery bug", {
  # mockery::stub(mockery_bug2, 'httr::GET', "GET value", depth=2)  # fails when mockery_bug2 calls `httr::GET`:
  # -> fails to mock (GET gets called): Failed to connect to 127.0.0.1 port 8000: Connection refused

  # mockery::stub(mockery_bug2, 'GET', "GET value", depth=2)  # works when mockery_bug2 calls `GET`:
  mockery::stub(mockery_bug2, 'GET', "GET value", depth=2)  # works when mockery_bug2 calls `GET`:
  # -> does mock (GET value is bad - as expected): no applicable method for 'status_code' applied to an object of class "character"

  mockery_bug()
})
```

title: mock missing arguments?
description:
I tried:

```r
f <- function(x) {}
g <- function(x) f(x = x)
```

When I invoke `g()`, it returns NULL with no error.

With mock as the following, it raises an error:

```r
m <- mock()
with_mock(f = m, g())
```

```
Error in f(x = x) : argument "x" is missing, with no default 
```

It seems that mockery does not support missing arguments.

I suggest that mockery assert missing arguments using `alist` such as the following:

```r
with_mock(f = m, {
  actual <- g()
  expect_args(m, 1, alist(x = ))  # assert missing
})
```

title: Make website
stubing does not propagate into partialised function
description:
Not sure there is a way to overcome this limitation but it would make the package more useful if you would allow to also mock functions that were partialised with purrr like this:
``` r
library(testthat)
plus <- function(x = 0, y = 0) {
  x + y
}

x_times_two <- function(x, y) {
  plus(x, x)
}

contains_plus <- purrr::partial(x_times_two, x = 3) # contains a call to plus()

mockery::stub(
  x_times_two,
  "plus", function(x, y) -1111
)

expect_equal(contains_plus(y = 2), -1111)
#> Error: contains_plus(y = 2) not equal to -1111.
#> 1/1 mismatches
#> [1] 6 - -1111 == 1117


mockery::stub(
  contains_plus,
  "plus", function(x, y) -1111
)
expect_equal(contains_plus(y = 2), -1111)
#> Error: contains_plus(y = 2) not equal to -1111.
#> 1/1 mismatches
#> [1] 6 - -1111 == 1117
```

title: stub and mock functions fail in functions that use the magrittr pipe
description:
``` r
library(magrittr)

add <- function(a, b) a + b
identity <- function(a) a
increment_chained <- function(a) identity(a) %>% add(1)
increment_assigned <- function(a) { x <- identity(a); add(x) }

testthat::test_that('chained stubbed functions work', {
  mock_chained <- mockery::mock(10)
  mockery::stub(increment_chained, 'identity', mock_chained)
  mockery::stub(increment_chained, 'add', 99)
  
  result <- increment_chained(1)
  testthat::expect_equal(result, 99)
  mockery::expect_called(mock_chained, 1)
})
#> ── FAILURE (<text>:15:3): chained stubbed functions work ───────────────────────
#> mock object has not been called 1 time

testthat::test_that('sequential stubbed functions work', {
  mock_assigned <- mockery::mock(10)
  mockery::stub(increment_assigned, 'identity', mock_assigned)
  mockery::stub(increment_assigned, 'add', 99)
  
  result <- increment_assigned(1)
  testthat::expect_equal(result, 99)
  mockery::expect_called(mock_assigned, 1)
})
#> Test passed 🥇
```

title: Multiple stub/mocks within a function fails at depth >= 2
description:
There appears to be a bug with r-lib/mockery `expect_called()` and `stub()` for multiple functions at depth >=2. `stub()` and `expect_called()` works as expected for multiple functions at a depth of 1. At depth >= 2, the first stubbed/mocked function (A) is called (works as expected), but the subsequent stubbed/mocked functions (B,C,...) are not called, instead the actual function is called. Either there is a bug, or I do not understand something. :-)

Please see my [project demonstrating the behavior](https://github.com/kbaynes/R-mockery-test).

Example: `mD2A` mock is called, but `mD2B` is not called.

```
    print("can stub multiple functions at depth=2")
    source("multiFuncD2.R")
    mD2A <- mock(TRUE)
    mD2B <- mock(TRUE)
    stub(Depth0.myFunction,'Depth2.myFunctionA',mD2A,depth=2)
    stub(Depth0.myFunction,'Depth2.myFunctionB',mD2B,depth=2)
    Depth0.myFunction()
    expect_called(mD2A,1)
    expect_called(mD2B,1)
```

title: Stubbing out S4 methods
description:
I'm trying to test a package with a number of S4 generics and methods. Example code:

```r
## Code
readAFileFun <- function(path) {
    header <- "I read a file!"
    c(header, readLines(con = path))
}

## this is the same as above, but is a generic with a method instead of a function
setGeneric("readAFile", function(path) standardGeneric("readAFile"))
setMethod("readAFile", "character", function(path) {
    header <- "I read a file!"
    readLines(con = path)
})
```

Tests using testthat:

```r
test_that("stub generic s4", {
    mockery::stub(readAFileFun, "readLines", "Not really a file!")
    lines <- readAFileFun("File paths don't matter!")
    expect(length(lines), 2)  # this works perfectly

    mockery::stub(readAFile, "readLines", "Not really a file!")
    lines <- readAFile("File paths don't matter!")
    expect(length(lines), 2)
})
```

The error I'm seeing is `Error: unable to find an inherited method for function 'readAFile' for signature '"character"`. I'm not entirely certain what's going on, but it looks like the stub is interfering with R's method dispatching.

title: How to stub Shiny observers?
Double-colon mocking not working at depth
description:
Here's my reprex, showing a failed attempt at mocking: ``` r library(mockery) func <- function() { .request("http://google.com") } .request <- function(url) { RCurl::getURL(url) } mock_response = mock("foo") stub(func, 'RCurl::getURL', mock_response, depth=5) print(func()) #> [1] "\n301 Moved\n

301 Moved

\nThe document has moved\nhere.\r\n\r\n" ``` Created on 2021-09-17 by the [reprex package](https://reprex.tidyverse.org) (v2.0.1) If I change to mocking an imported function instead, it works as desired: ``` r library(mockery) library(RCurl) func <- function() { .request("http://google.com") } .request <- function(url) { getURL(url) } mock_response = mock("foo") stub(func, 'getURL', mock_response, depth=5) print(func()) #> [1] "foo" ``` Alternatively, if I only need to go 1 level deep, **and I remove the `depth=5` argument**, it also works as desired: ``` r library(mockery) func <- function() { RCurl::getURL("http://google.com") } mock_response = mock("foo") stub(func, 'RCurl::getURL', mock_response) print(func()) #> [1] "foo" ``` If the `depth=5` argument is included (which theoretically should have no effect here), it fails: ``` r library(mockery) func <- function() { RCurl::getURL("http://google.com") } mock_response = mock("foo") stub(func, 'RCurl::getURL', mock_response, depth=5) print(func()) #> [1] "\n301 Moved\n

301 Moved

\nThe document has moved\nhere.\r\n\r\n" ```

title: Unintuative stub/mock behaviour
description:
I apologies in advance if this is "expected behaviour" or I am being dim but how `stub` and `mock` work doesn't seem that intuative to me :( 

```
library(mockery)
f <- function() 1
g <- function() f() + 1
h <- function() g() + 1
i <- function() h() + 1
j <- function() i() + 1

mocky <- mock(100, 200)
stub(j, "f", mocky, depth = 2)
j()
#> [1] 104

mocky <- mock(300, 400)
stub(j, "f", mocky, depth = 2)
j()
#> [1] 204
```
> Created on 2021-11-30 by the reprex package (v2.0.1)

* How come the mocking was successful, the `f()` function is called at depth 4 so I wouldn't have expected `depth = 2` to have replaced it. If it is a global replace (at all depths) would it make more sense to convert this to a logical called `recursive` or something similar? 

* I am confused as to why after both overwriting the `mocky` object and re-running `stub()` it still returns the value from the first mocked object ? If I re-run the code to define the functions it works as intended but this isn't really possible when dealing with test_that code

If this is indeed expected behaviour would it be possible to update the documentation to explain why it behaves this way ?

title: Mockery not cleaning up after itself properly
description:
Hi,

I'm really not sure what the exactly what is going here but I am running into a bug where due to a combination of using a package + exporting functions mockery isn't cleaning up after itself. I managed to create the smallest repex of the problem that I could manage here: https://github.com/gowerc/test-mockery

For reference the main unit tests in that repo are:

```
test_that("test - 1",  {
    x <- 1
    class(x) <- "meth"
    mocky <- mockery::mock(2)
    mockery::stub(main, "some_other_fun", mocky, depth = 2)
    expect_equal(main(x), 2)
})


test_that("test - 2",  {
    expect_equal(get_list_of_fun(), list("myfun" = somefun))
})
```

When calling `devtools::test()` on that project I get:

```
==> devtools::test()

ℹ Loading testMock
ℹ Testing testMock
✓ | F W S  OK | Context
x | 1       1 | mock                                                                                                   
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Failure (test-mock.R:12:5): test - 2
get_list_of_fun() (`actual`) not equal to list(myfun = somefun) (`expected`).

`environment(actual$myfun)` is <env:0x7f9ac07c5b00>
`environment(expected$myfun)` is <env:namespace:testMock>
───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

══ Results ════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
[ FAIL 1 | WARN 0 | SKIP 0 | PASS 1 ]
```

Note that the error is coming from "test -2" which doesn't use mockery i.e. the changes mockery has made in the first unit test have bled over to the second unit test.  My expectation (sorry if I have this wrong) was that any changes made by mockery should be localised to the specific `test_that()` block.

title: mockery::mock() can't easily mock functions which defuse their arguments
description:
Hello guys,

I've encounteres the issue, that a mock-object, created by `mockery::mock()` can't handle functions which defuse their arguments:

```
my_function <- function(...) {
  dots <- rlang::enexprs(...)
  print(dots)
}

my_function(some_none_object)
# [[1]]
# some_none_object

my_wrapper <- function(...) {
  my_function(...)
}

my_wrapper(some_none_object)
# [[1]]
# some_none_object
```
If I now test my function without any arguments, the test passes without failure.
```
describe("my_wrapper", {
  it("calls my_function", {
    mock_my_function <- mockery::mock("it does!")
    mockery::stub(my_wrapper, "my_function", mock_my_function)

    expect_equal(my_wrapper(), "it does!")
    mockery::expect_called(mock_my_function, 1)
  })
})
# No issues here, as no arguments were passed via ...
```

But, I test it with an argument given, I get this error.
```
describe("my_wrapper", {
  it("calls my_function", {
    mock_my_function <- mockery::mock("it does!")
    mockery::stub(my_wrapper, "my_function", mock_my_function)

    expect_equal(my_wrapper(some_none_object), "it does!")
    mockery::expect_called(mock_my_function, 1)
  })
})
# -- Error (Line 6): my_wrapper: calls my_function -------------------------------
#   Error in `my_function(...)`: object 'some_none_object' not found
# Backtrace:
#   1. testthat::expect_equal(my_wrapper(some_none_object), "it does!")
# 4. drkleinrkprovisionentool::my_wrapper(some_none_object)
# 5. mockery my_function(...)
# at drkleinrkprovisionentool/R/test_mockery.R:11:2
```
The reason for this error might be found in `mockery::mock`
```
function (..., cycle = FALSE, envir = parent.frame()) 
{
    stopifnot(is.environment(envir))
    return_values <- eval(substitute(alist(...)))  # <- right here. It does not defuse arguments.
    return_values_env <- envir
    call_no <- 0
    calls <- list()
[...]
```

My workaround / solution to this is atm something like the following. I must admit, that I am not 100% familiar with the whole `rlang:expr, rlang::enexpr, rlang::exprs, etc... ` family of functions yet, but it does work:
```
describe("my_wrapper", {
  it("calls my_function", {
    mock_my_function <- mockery::mock("it does!")
    mockery::stub(my_wrapper, "my_function", function(...) {
      dots <- rlang::exprs(...)
      mock_my_function(rlang::expr((!!!dots)))
    })

    expect_equal(my_wrapper(some_none_object), "it does!")
    mockery::expect_called(mock_my_function, 1)
    mockery::expect_args(mock_my_function, 1, quote((some_none_object)))
  })
})
# Test passed
```
Even though, my expectations must be adopted a little bit to the workarround...


Might there be a solution to this?

Maybe in the form of a 2nd mock() funtcion, which uses defusing operators instead of `substitute`? Or an optional argument like:
use_tidy_semantics = TRUE ?

That would be great! :)

title: When `depth=2` mocks persist between test_that blocks
description:
Thank you for your great work on the package.
I realized an issue when we stab function with `depth=2` in two separate `test_that` blocks:

```
# test-hello.R
sq <- function(z) {
  z ^ 2
}
sq_diff <- function(a, b) {
  sq(a - b)
}
point_dist <- function(x, y) {
  sqrt(sq_diff(x[1], y[1]) + sq_diff(x[2], y[2]))
}

test_that("mocks depth=2 should be applied", {
  sq_mock <- function(z) 2
  mockery::stub(point_dist, 'sq', sq_mock, depth = 2)
  expect_equal(point_dist(c(0, -2), c(0, 2)), 2)
})

test_that("mocks depth=2 shouldn't be applied anymore", {
  expect_equal(point_dist(c(0, -2), c(0, 2)), 4)
})
```

While running the second block, we realize the specified mocks still persist (it happens only for `depth>=2`):
```
> testthat::test_file("test-hello.R")
[1] "helper"
[ FAIL 1 | WARN 0 | SKIP 0 | PASS 1 ]

── Failure (test-hello.R:33:3): mocks depth=2 shouldn't be applied anymore ─────
point_dist(c(0, -2), c(0, 2)) (`actual`) not equal to 4 (`expected`).

  `actual`: 2
`expected`: 4
[ FAIL 1 | WARN 0 | SKIP 0 | PASS 1 ]
```

What's more I was trying to "force unmock" the function in the first block with:
```
test_that("mocks depth=2 should be applied", {
  sq_mock <- function(z) 2
  mockery::stub(point_dist, 'sq', sq_mock, depth = 2)
  expect_equal(point_dist(c(0, -2), c(0, 2)), 2)
  mockery::stub(point_dist, 'sq', sq, depth = 2)
})
```
but the second block still uses the mocked version.

The only solution is to "unmock" directly in the second block:
```
test_that("mocks depth=2 shouldn't be applied anymore", {
  mockery::stub(point_dist, 'sq', sq, depth = 2)
  expect_equal(point_dist(c(0, -2), c(0, 2)), 4)
})
```

I'd be grateful if you could take a look at the issue. Thank you.

title: depth not working? cannot change value of locked binding for '.onLoad'
description:
I have a package (https://github.com/MichaelChirico/geohashTools) where several functions rely on Suggested packages.

At the top of such functions, I do a `requireNamespace(pkg)` check & error if the Suggested package isn't installed.

Earlier, I was doing coverage tests for these by (e.g. for function `foo`)

```
stub(foo, requireNamespace, FALSE)
testthat::expect_error(foo(x), 'please install')
```

There are enough functions like this now that I split off this test into a helper function (_unexported_):

```
check_suggested = function(pkg) {
  if (!requireNamespace(pkg, quietly = TRUE)) {
    stop("This function requires an installation of ", pkg,
         "; install.packages('", pkg, "') to proceed.")
  }
}
```

The old tests fail, I assume because the stubbing is only done _directly_ in the environment of `foo`, so when `foo` calls `check_suggested`, `requireNamespace` operates as normal.

So I tried to stub `check_suggested`:

```
stub(geohashTools:::check_suggested, requireNamespace, FALSE)
```

But this didn't work -- the code `foo(x)` runs without error.

Then I came across the `depth` argument which looked promising, but it's giving me a strange error:

```
stub(geohashTools:::check_suggested, 'requireNamespace', FALSE, depth = 2L)
```

> Error in assign(where_name, func, parent_env) : 
  cannot change value of locked binding for '.onLoad'

Am I using the argument wrong? How should I go about stubbing in this case to mock an environment where a suggested package is not installed?

title: `with_stubs()`/`local_stubs()`
description:
Now that `testthat`s own `with_mock()`/`local_mock()` are going the way of the dodo, I was wondering whether it might be useful to expand the API of `mockery` a bit. What I was having in mind, was something like

* `stubs()`: which basically does what was suggested in #37, i.e. provides a mechanism for stubbing out multiple functions, i.e. like

    ```r
    stubs(
      where,
      `namespace::fun_1` = replacement_1,
      `namespace::fun_2` = replacement_2
    )
    ```

* `with_stubs()`/`local_stubs() `: maybe this could also be part of `withr`, idk, but going with the test-fixtures flow, this would power something like

    ```r
    with_stubs(
      where,
      `namespace::fun_1` = replacement_1,
      `namespace::fun_2` = replacement_2,
      {
        expect_something(where(some_arg))
        expect_other(where(other_arg))
      }
    )
    ```

    or of course

    ```r
    local_stubs(where, fun_1 = replacement_1, fun_2 = replacement_2)
    expect_something(where(some_arg))
    expect_other(where(other_arg))
    ```

    where the stubbed out functions are reverted back to the original functions (using for example `withr::defer()`)

I have started putting something together for my own use and I am happy to share and discuss here and/or open a PR. Of course only if there is interest in this and if such an obvious extension is not already under works.

title: Multiple stubs
description:
First of all, `stub()` is wonderful! Easy to use, intuitive, just great. :clap: 
I searched how to stub multiple functions and I was struggling on it. Then, I found it, just use `stub()` twice:

```r
f <- function(date = Sys.Date()) {
    print(date)
    readline("Get your opinion about!")
  }  
stub(where = f, what = 'Sys.Date', how = as.Date('1900-01-01'))
stub(where = f, what = 'readline', how = "Nice!")
```
Is there a way to improve this? Allowing vectors for `what` and `how` maybe?
Something like:
```r
stub(where = f,
     what = c('Sys.Date', 'readline'),
     how = c(as.Date('1900-01-01'), "Nice!"))
```
Anyway, I think that adding a double stubbing example in documentation could help. What do you think about it? Many thanks!

title: Double colon stubbed function name + double colon assignment = cryptic parsing bug
description:
I wish I could have crafted a more comprehensible title, but this is a weird bug. Here's a reproducible example:

```r
library(testthat)
library(mockery)

myFunc <- function() {
  x <- c(a=42)
  names(x) # this works fine
  names(x) <- 'b' # so does this
  base::names(x) # and this
  base::names(x) <- 'b' # <--------------------------------------- here it breaks
  return(42)
}

test_that('most stubs work fine', {
  stub(myFunc, 'singleColon:trash_works_fine', TRUE)
  expect_equal(myFunc(), 42)
})

test_that('double colon in stubbed function breaks', {
  stub(myFunc, 'doubleColon::triggers_cryptic_bug', TRUE)
  expect_equal(myFunc(), 42)
})
```

The indicated line produces the following error:
```r
Error: Test failed: 'double colon in mocked function breaks'
* <text>:2:0: unexpected end of input
1: base::names<-
   ^
1: expect_equal(myFunc(), 42) at ~/.active-rstudio-document:21
2: quasi_label(enquo(object), label)
3: eval_bare(get_expr(quo), get_env(quo))
4: myFunc()
5: base::`names<-` at ~/.active-rstudio-document:9
6: eval(parse(text = code), eval_env)
7: parse(text = code)
```

I found this bug in testing my own package, where another `<package>::function<-` statement (not `base::names<-`) gave me the same "unexpected end of input" error. It took me a while to even figure out it was mockery that was causing the problem, since it doesn't appear anywhere in the stacktrace.

title: add in-place stub_primitive
description:
if one needs to replace (stub) a primitive in function pkg1::A that is called from pkg2::B neither `stub()` nor `with_mock()` will suffice

one way:

- find the function under test - we want to intercept calls originating from this function; name it X
- unlock environment which function X belongs to
- add a new entry in this unlocked environment named after the primitive we want to mock
- lock the environment


it can be done in pure R as well but requires additional environment:

- take a copy of function X
- put this copy in a new environment whose parent is the env of X
- add the intercept for the primitive in the new env
- unlock binding for original X in its env
- replace X with its copy
- lock binding

the second method is more complex and makes it a bit more difficult to replace the same primitive in subsequent calls or to replace multiple primitives

title: Allow user to specify depth of stubbing
description:
At the moment, the stub`stub` function only stubs out the function to be stubbed if it is directly called from the target function.

We should introduce an optional parameter to `stub` that allows the user to specify how deep they want to the stub to be active. E.g. a `stub(some_func, 'other_func', 100, depth=2)` would indicate that `other_func` should be stubbed with something that returns 100 not only if called directly from `some_func`, but also if called by something that `some_func` calls.
